title: Searching an Array
objectives: Find whether an element is in an array and where it is

hook.text: Is "Alice" in a student list, and if so, at what position? To find out, you need to CHECK the array from start to end.

concept.heading: The logic of linear search
concept.body: Linear search walks through the array from start to end and compares each element with the target value. If a match is found, that index is recorded. If no match is found by the time the array ends, the element is NOT in the array.

concept.heading: The not-found case
concept.body: Before the search begins, you prepare a "found" (or "position ← -1") variable. It is updated if a match is found during the loop. If this variable is still at its starting value when the loop ends, the element is not in the array.

workedExamples.prompt: Find whether the number 30 is in an array and, if it is, its index.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
numbers ← [10, 20, 30, 40]
position ← -1
FOR i ← 0 TO 3 STEP 1
  IF numbers[i] = 30
    position ← i
  END
END_LOOP
WRITE position

steps.explain: position is set to -1, meaning "not found yet".
When i = 2, numbers[2] = 30 matches, and position ← 2.
Result: position = 2 (30 was found at index 2).

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: "Dan" is the 3rd element (index 2) of the names array.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen (the target value is not in the array)?
exercises.hint: 99 is not in the array, so position is never updated.

exercises.question: What does it mean if the "position" variable is still -1 after the loop ends?
options: The target element was not found in the array
The first element was being searched for

feedback.correct: Correct. If position stays at its starting value (-1), no match was found.
feedback.incorrect: -1 is the "not found yet" starting value. If it is still -1 at the end of the loop, the element is not in the array.

exercises.question: Put the steps of the linear search algorithm in the correct order.
steps: Walk through the array from start to end
Compare each element with the target value
If there is a match, record the position

exercises.question: How many comparisons does a linear search make in the worst case in an array of N elements?

feedback.correct: Correct. If the element is not in the array or is at the very end, all N elements are checked.
feedback.incorrect: In the worst case (the element is missing or at the end), a linear search checks all N elements.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: Searching for an element by checking an array one element at a time from start to end is called ___ search.

summary: Linear search walks through the array from start to end and compares each element with the target value.
Starting with "position ← -1" stands for the "not found" case.
In the worst case, N comparisons are made in an array of N elements.
